title: Compact objects form a thick subcategory
statement: For a pretriangulated category with set-indexed coproducts [def-weil-triangulated-category], the object property of being compact [def-pc-compact-object] is triangulated (contains zero, is stable under integer shifts and under distinguished triangles) and stable under retracts. Compactness is for the indexing universe of the given coproducts.

proof.text: The zero object is compact [def-pc-compact-object]: all its Hom groups vanish, so both the direct sum of Hom groups and Hom into any coproduct are zero. Shifts are compact by the shift-inverse adjunction, additive Hom equivalences and coproduct comparison, by importing the single proved compact_shift theorem from CompactCone [lem-sc-compact-cone].

A retract K of L is compact when L is compact [def-pc-compact-object]. Precomposition with the inclusion and retraction gives retractions on the direct sums of Hom groups and on Hom into the coproduct. Naturality of the comparison makes these commute. Injectivity descends from L after precomposition with the retraction and cancellation by the inclusion; surjectivity lifts a map through L and precomposes its finite-supported preimage with the inclusion. Thus compactness is stable under retracts and consequently under isomorphisms. The comparison naturality theorem is imported from CompactCone, not proved again.

Closure under third terms of distinguished triangles is [lem-sc-compact-cone]. Together with shift closure, triangle rotation gives closure under middle terms, via ObjectProperty.IsTriangulatedClosed₂.of_isTriangulatedClosed₃. The zero, shift, and middle-term classes assemble into ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated; the already proved retract class gives the second conclusion.

lean.statement:
theorem compactObjects_isThick
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ]
    [Preadditive C] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive]
    [Pretriangulated C] [HasCoproducts.{w} C] :
    ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated (fun K : C ↦ IsCompactObject K) ∧
      ObjectProperty.IsStableUnderRetracts (fun K : C ↦ IsCompactObject K)
